channel.title: Insights by Christopher R. H. Hanusa
channel.description: Writings by Christopher R. H. Hanusa about math, art, coding, teaching, leadership, academia, and other miscellaneous topics

item.title: Reimagining hanusa.xyz
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: I’ve renewed my website for 2026, including a refreshed feel and an integrated blog. How did it happen and what can you expect from the update?

item.title: Bridges 2024
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: Hyperbolic Emergence in the Bridges 2024 art exhibition, a talk on Fractal Emergence, and Apollonian jewelry on the fashion show runway.

item.title: A Talk on Mathematical Design
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: My talk on the Mathematical Design course in the math art minisymposium of the German Mathematical Society’s annual meeting.

item.title: Teaching Mathematical Design
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: A semester of Mathematical Design, where non-math majors learn functions in Desmos and turn them into art on AxiDraw pen plotters.

item.title: Teaching 3D Design and 3D Printing
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: An article on teaching 3D design and 3D printing in the classroom, with a case study and an appendix of Mathematica design techniques.

item.title: Packing 16 Tetrahedra in Mathematica
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: Exploring the optimal packing of 16 tetrahedra, and cleaning up the model in Mathematica to reveal its interior structure.

item.title: Riemondrian and Calculus Art
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: A look back at Riemondrian, a mashup of Riemann sums and Mondrian, and the student work, jewelry, and prints it has inspired.

item.title: Existence and Uniqueness: A Solo Show
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: My solo show at Gallery 1064, featuring three collections of 3D-printed sculptures: Riemannscapes, Window Evolution, and Streamlines.

item.title: Streamlines Sculptures at JMM 2022
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: My 3D-printed Streamlines sculptures, which trace the paths of particles through vector fields, at the JMM 2022 art exhibition.

item.title: From Parametric to Polar in Desmos
item.dc:creator: Christopher R. H. Hanusa
item.description: How to wrap a parametric curve around a circle in Desmos, by shifting it up and applying a polar transformation.
